punchline: The Harvard study that followed 724 men for decades found that closeness predicted health better than the numbers people chased.
thirty_sec: The Harvard Study of Adult Development has followed 724 men since the late 1930s. Robert Waldinger and Marc Schulz report that the strength of people's relationships predicts the health of body and brain as they age. Waldinger has said that satisfaction with relationships at fifty predicted health at eighty better than cholesterol did.
